text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- President Arpad Goncz's trip to Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Mexico has been a success, as major progress has been made in diplomatic, economic and cultural relations, said presidential spokesman Andras Farago.

- Hungarian tourists will soon be able to travel to Mexico and Japan without visas. Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szent-Ivanyi also said the costs of admission to NATO could reach HUF eight billion to 10 billion annually for ten years.

- Parliament yesterday began debate on proposed amendments to the Penal Code and later accepted a proposal under which Olympic champions over 35 years of age will draw an annuity equivalent the average income of those living on wages and salaries.

- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze and Secret Services Minister Istvan Nikolits on Tuesday agreed that the issue of responsibility for the loss of ten tonnes of banknote paper suitable for producing forged banknotes, cannot be established, due to lack of evidence.

- Slovakia asked the International Court of Justice to establish that Hungary had no right to call off the joint project of the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros hydropower plant and is obliged to refund losses it has caused. However, the Slovak request also said that it is possible to modify the 1977 treaty with the consensus of the two parties.

- The central budget deficit for the first quarter totalled HUF 113.1 billion, 31 percent of the projected annual figure. Social security system deficit already surpassed the planned annual sum of HUF 13 billion by late March.
- The insurance company Nationale Nederlanden Hungary Rt has introduced a new product combining life insurance with investments in securities, said president and CEO Gyorgy Bordas.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Criminals possessing several tonnes of special paper used for printing bank notes have attempted to blackmail the Hungarian state. The crooks threatened to hand over the consignment to their Ukrainian colleagues, who would then flood the country with counterfeit HUF 5,000 notes unless their demand for several billion forints was met. Seven suspects have already been arrested.

- Militant farmers' group, the Agricultural Producers' Advocacy Association (Metesz) will organise a nationwide boycott of Takarekbank and its associated savings cooperatives if the bank's privatisation is not stopped, Metesz leader said.
- A giant cement production company with 50 percent of the country's total capacity was formed yesterday with the merger of Dunai Cementgyar and Beremendi Cementgyar.
- The after-tax profit of Volksbank Hungary Rt grew sevenfold, from HUF 11.4 million to HUF 80.8 million last year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn departs today for a tour of Singapore and Malaysia.

- The contract of sale for a 25 percent plus one vote stake in the Budapest Waterworks was signed yesterday by the Budapest Council and a consortium of Lyonnaise des Eaux S.A. of France and Germany's RWE Aqua GmbH.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- An attorney representing Short Missile Systems Monday submitted an application to the Ombudsman for Data Protection, objecting to the fact that the Defence Ministry refuses to provide information on when the Procurement Office formed to handle the tender was registered.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
